mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days across all monetary regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 9.0% signals severe labor market weakness, triggering immediate equity sell-offs due to reduced consumer spending confidence, producing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% over one month indicate collapsing consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing output below 90.0 (INDPRO < 90.0) indicates a severe supply-side slowdown, reducing corporate earnings growth and generating negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 90.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strengthening labor market (PAYEMS increasing > 0.5% monthly) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases > 0.5% in 1 month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Core inflation exceeding 2.5% annually (CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5%) signals imminent monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annual change > 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in real GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% over six months indicate broad economic deterioration, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST decline > 0.5% in 6 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 0.5% in 6 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low inflation (CPIAUCSL annual change < 1.5%) combined with ultra-low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) creates optimal conditions for equity appreciation, yielding positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL annual change < 1.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
